title: הפוך גדול, בבקשה
synopsis: On their way to work, Khaled and Masha stop at a coffee kiosk in the street, and Liat takes their order. The kiosk doesn't have everything Khaled wants.

lines.en: Good morning! What would you like?
I'd like a latte, please.
Large or small?
Large. How much is it?
Fifteen shekels. Anything else?
Yes, can I have a chocolate croissant?

lines.he: סליחה, אין קרואסון שוקולד. יש רק חמאה.
lines.en: Sorry, there are no chocolate croissants. There are only butter ones.

lines.he: אין בעיה, אז חמאה. מאשה, מה את שותה?
lines.en: No problem, butter then. Masha, what are you drinking?

lines.he: אני לא שותה קפה. אפשר תה עם נענע?
lines.en: I don't drink coffee. Can I have tea with mint?
Of course. Altogether that's forty shekels.
I'm paying. Can I pay by card?

lines.he: בטח. הנה הקפה, התה והקרואסון. בתיאבון!
lines.en: Sure. Here's the coffee, the tea and the croissant. Enjoy!

questions.qEn: How much does a large latte cost?

tf.why: Liat says אין קרואסון שוקולד, יש רק חמאה, so Khaled takes a butter croissant.
She says אני לא שותה קפה and asks for tea with mint.
Masha pays: she says אני משלמת and asks to pay by credit card.
Liat says ביחד זה ארבעים שקלים, 'altogether that's forty shekels'.

expressions.note: רוצה is spelled the same for a man and a woman, but a man says ani rotsé and a woman says ani rotsá. קפה הפוך, literally 'upside-down coffee', is the standard Israeli milky coffee; you can simply order הפוך גדול.
עולה = costs (literally 'goes up'). For the total of several things, ask כמה זה ביחד?

expressions.en: Can I have...? / Is it possible to...?
expressions.note: With a noun it asks for something: אפשר קרואסון? אפשר תה? With an infinitive it asks permission: אפשר לשלם באשראי? Masha shortens this to אפשר באשראי? (by credit card).
What every seller asks. Answer כן, and add what you want, or לא, זהו, תודה (no, that's it, thanks).
Literally 'there is no problem'. A relaxed way to accept a change, or to answer סליחה or תודה.
Pronounced bete'avón, literally 'with appetite'. Said by whoever serves the food, and by people at the table before they eat.

title: הדירה החדשה של רנא
synopsis: Rana has just moved into a new apartment and shows her friend Gil around. Gil likes what he sees, until he finds out who gets the second bedroom.

lines.he: ברוך הבא, גיל! זאת הדירה החדשה שלי.
lines.en: Welcome, Gil! This is my new apartment.

lines.he: וואו, יפה! כמה חדרים יש פה?
lines.en: Wow, nice! How many rooms are there?
Three: a living room and two bedrooms.

lines.he: הסלון גדול! ויש מזגן? בקיץ פה חם מאוד.
lines.en: The living room is big! And is there air conditioning? It's very hot here in the summer.
There's an air conditioner in the living room. In the bedrooms there isn't.
And this is the kitchen? It's very small!
True, but there's a new fridge.
And is this your room?

lines.he: כן. והחדר השני הוא של מיצי.
lines.en: Yes. And the other room is Mitzi's.
Mitzi? You have a roommate?
No! Mitzi is my cat.

lines.he: לחתולה יש חדר? ובדירה שלי אני ישן בסלון!
lines.en: The cat has a room? And in my apartment, I sleep in the living room!

questions.q: כמה חדרים יש בדירה של רנא?
questions.qEn: How many rooms are there in Rana's apartment?
questions.answer: יש שלושה חדרים: סלון ושני חדרי שינה.
questions.answerEn: There are three rooms: a living room and two bedrooms.

questions.qEn: Where is there an air conditioner?
questions.answerEn: There's an air conditioner only in the living room.

tf.why: She welcomes Gil with זאת הדירה החדשה שלי, 'this is my new apartment'.

tf.sEn: There's an air conditioner in every room.
tf.why: Rana says בסלון יש מזגן, בחדרים אין: only the living room has one.
Gil says הוא קטן מאוד, 'it's very small', and Rana agrees: נכון.

tf.sEn: There's a new fridge in the kitchen.
tf.why: Rana answers נכון, אבל יש מקרר חדש, 'true, but there's a new fridge'.

expressions.note: Said to a guest at the door. To a woman: ברוכה הבאה! To a group: ברוכים הבאים!
Israelis count the living room as a room: a דירת שלושה חדרים has a living room and two bedrooms. Bedroom = חדר שינה, plural חדרי שינה.

expressions.en: There's an air conditioner in the living room. In the bedrooms there isn't.
expressions.note: יש = there is / there are, אין = there isn't / there aren't. Neither one changes for gender or number, and in a short answer each can stand alone: יש מזגן? – אין.
של comes after the noun, and the noun takes ה: החדר שלך, החתולה שלי. An adjective goes between them: הדירה החדשה שלי.
יש ל + person = to have: יש לי, יש לך, לחתולה יש חדר. The negative is אין לי. שותף (m, shutáf) / שותפה (f, shutafá) is a flatmate, and also a business partner.

title: איפה הדואר?
synopsis: Emily needs the post office, but she doesn't know the neighbourhood yet. She stops a passer-by, Adisu, and asks him the way.

lines.en: Excuse me, do you know where the post office is?
The post office? Yes, it's on Herzl Street.
Is it far from here?
No, five minutes on foot.
How do I get there?
You go straight as far as the traffic light.
Straight to the traffic light. And then?
At the light you turn left, and then right.
Left, then right. And the post office is there?
Yes, next to the bank, opposite the supermarket.
Thank you so much! I'm new here.

lines.he: בכיף! גם אני הולך לדואר. בואי איתי.
lines.en: My pleasure! I'm going to the post office too. Come with me.

questions.qEn: Which street is the post office on?
questions.answerEn: The post office is on Herzl Street.

questions.qEn: How long does it take to walk to the post office?
How do you get from here to the post office?
questions.answer: הולכים ישר עד הרמזור, ברמזור פונים שמאלה, ואז ימינה.
questions.answerEn: You go straight to the traffic light, left at the light, and then right.

tf.sEn: The post office is very far away.
tf.why: Adisu says it's חמש דקות ברגל, 'five minutes on foot'.

tf.sEn: At the traffic light you turn right.
tf.why: At the light you turn left: ברמזור פונים שמאלה. Only after that do you turn right.

tf.sEn: The post office is next to the bank.
tf.why: Adisu says ליד הבנק, מול הסופר, 'next to the bank, opposite the supermarket'.

tf.sEn: Adisu is going to the post office too.
tf.why: At the end he says גם אני הולך לדואר and invites Emily to come with him.

expressions.en: Excuse me, do you know where... is?
expressions.note: The polite way to stop someone in the street. To a woman: סליחה, את יודעת איפה הדואר?

A plural verb with no subject means 'you' or 'people' in general: איך הולכים לדואר? Directions use the same form: הולכים ישר, פונים שמאלה. You will also often hear איך מגיעים ל...? (how do you get to...?). לשם = to there; for 'there' alone say שם.

expressions.en: straight on / to the right / to the left
expressions.note: ימין and שמאל are the sides (right, left). With the ending ה they mean 'towards': פונים ימינה (yamína) = you turn right, פונים שמאלה (smóla) = you turn left. ישר (yashár) = straight on.
ברגל (barégel) = on foot, literally 'by leg'. The number is feminine because דקה (minute) is feminine: חמש דקות, שתי דקות.
Two small words for describing where a place is: הדואר ליד הבנק, מול הסופר. The street name comes with ב: ברחוב הרצל = on Herzl Street.
A warm, casual answer to תודה, pronounced bekéf. It also means 'sure, happy to' when someone asks a favour.
